record.body:
FULL-SITE-PROCESS unit 1a: every child of a site process in a nested domain of its own. This fixes SECURITY-DEBT `FSP-NESTLESS1`, found by unit 0 and recorded at lichen-adversary's check, E3.

- **`call-join`** (`lichen-sandbox/src/sandbox.rs`, `run_join`) runs the children an interpreter or mdBook starts: Lua's `io.popen` and `os.execute`, and mdBook's `book.toml` preprocessor and renderer commands.
  - It joined its call's group and took its filter, but entered no Landlock domain, so these children shared the site process's.
  - Landlock's signal scope does not separate a domain from itself, so they could signal the site process. Probe f measured it; the site process is granted no `/proc`, so `environ` and `fd/*` were already refused.
  - It now enters the same nested domain every other ordinary child gets (`enter_nested_domain`, A7), before the call's filter, when the site process is confined. It fails closed: a child that cannot enter it runs nothing.
- **The terminal's shell** is now found on the site process's `PATH`, with no child (`shell/pty.rs`, `resolve_shell`). A `which bash` run for it was an ordinary `.output()` with no domain at all.

This is the first sub-unit of unit 1, within its budget: about 30 product lines.

---

body.original:
Awesome thank you. 

In my past lives, tracing has been blanketed via correlation ids, and where you want spans is where you tag it allowing groupings across all requests. This works really well when there is a "saga" in micro-service orchestration terms which I suspect a PDS would be subject too, or at least within my applications use-cases it could be helpful. To the point of comms I think a single span for notify would probably do, allowing a trace/coorlation id would be helpful for persisting a lexicon record and something go bump, or probably more realistically a CAR Export. I added a span for notifying a PDS user they had a lapsed subscription, in hindsight it was misguided and not the right tool for the job, yet the span made it possible for me to see that sending a notification to a bsky user failed in the noise of the logs.

record.body:
Runs the tactics epic's exit criterion: paired `--tactics live` against `--tactics engage` (every force pinned to Engage, which is the identity retune and therefore the pre-layer scoring) on identical scenarios and seeds. Three blocks of the representative suite, 224 games per arm per block, at seeds 15000, 15500 and 16000.

The result is a **null, with the point estimate slightly against the layer**: live won 141/216, 125/212 and 133/217; Engage won 142/217, 137/219 and 139/219. Paired over **630** common decided games, live 387 against Engage 402; 115 pairs were won by Engage only against 100 by live; McNemar **p = 0.34**. The enabled-minus-disabled estimate is about **-2.4 points**, inside the ~10-point same-code block variance measured in `harness.md`. The exit criterion ("a run where the layer is disabled loses by an interval that excludes zero") is **not met**.

So the layer ships as the transition/logging/measurement seam, not as a strength feature. The measured runs also carry the harness numbers: 99.8–99.9% of decisions answered, 17–23 defaults per 224 games, zero illegal orders, and both arms are the same build with only the scoring arm changed. Docs only; `plan/tactics.md` records the three blocks and the conclusion.

Adds a deterministic opponent and an integration harness: SDS on one side, a **scripted seat** on the other, a known seed, no Princess and no RNG. `ScriptClient` is a real `BotClient` subject to double-blind filtering; it defaults to hold still, hold fire and no torso twist, deploys deterministically at the first legal hex, and accepts an optional JSON plan of per-round move/fire orders keyed by entity id or unit name. A source test enforces that it never imports Princess or draws a random number, and a missing plan is rejected before a match starts. `sds/match.py` gains the `script` seat kind.

`./sds.sh integration scenarios/integration` plays each scenario at its configured seed and checks assertions against the result document: outcome, carried state, position/altitude/velocity, answered decisions, and weapons actually fired. Each assertion prints PASS/FAIL with the evidence line; any failure exits non-zero. First scenarios: **ba-mount** (Elemental mounts a Badger by round 3), **taxi** (Warrior H-7 moves from (7,2) to (3,13) with altitude held), **artillery-cannon-direct** (Sniper Cannon fires and the server records it). Current run: **9/9 assertions, exit 0**.

Building the taxi scenario found a real bug: fliers were deploying at elevation 0 and every forward step was refused. That fix is in the series. The artillery *landing* scenario is not authored yet, with the blockers recorded: `Observation.shotsAt` excludes `ArtilleryWeapon` tubes (a plain attack packet hangs the indirect handler), `turnsTilHit` is 0 inside 17 hexes so a one-sheet board lands the same round, and nothing yet carries an in-flight shell into the result ticks. Enemy shells are also client-filtered, as #504 records. `./scripts/build.sh`, the Rust workspace, 789 Python tests and `sds integration` pass.

record.body:
Adds a deterministic opponent and a tagged integration corpus: SDS on one side, a scripted seat on the other, a known seed, no Princess and no RNG. `ScriptClient` is a real `BotClient` subject to double-blind filtering; it holds still and holds fire by default, deploys deterministically, and accepts an optional JSON plan of per-round move/fire orders. The runner plays each scenario and asserts outcome, carried state, position/altitude, answered decisions and weapons fired; `--tag`, `--list` and `--json` select subsets, and every scenario must carry tags, rules metadata and a `should / why / determinism` block.

Twelve scenarios now cover battle armor (mount, Omnimek mount, ride/dismount), artillery (two direct cannon cases), VTOL (taxi/canyon crossing, elevation), and two normal baselines (Mek duel, vehicle lance). Current run: **33/33 assertions pass**. Two scenarios are recorded as blocked rather than silently skipped: indirect artillery landing (`turnsTilHit` is 0 inside a mapsheet, no TARGETING-phase path, no hex-target action) and VTOL altitude change (`steps_to` emits no UP/DOWN step). Both name the exact code gap. The harness also found and fixed a real bug on its first run: fliers deployed at elevation 0 and every forward step was refused.

The `determinism` block says what the seed guarantees and what may shift: with the scripted opponent, decisions are reproducible, but MegaMek's shot-resolution order is not pinned, so timed assertions are `byRound` bounds. One run under a saturation wave had a single timing assertion fail; the rerun passed 33/33, which is why the blocks are documented that way and the rules/version fields are present for the upcoming core-rules migration. 806 Python tests and `prek --all-files` pass.

record.body:
FULL-SITE-PROCESS unit 1b: `site_process_main`, the admin thread and the narrow sandbox. This is the plan's "containment in one place". Design: `machine-docs/plans/FULL-SITE-PROCESS-U0-DESIGN-2026-10-26.md`, checked SATISFIED.

A site process now starts in this order (`lichen-site/src/site_process/start.rs`). `lichen-cli`'s `main` hands it over after `preamble`.
1. **The admin thread** (`site_process/admin.rs`) starts first, so it keeps the site process's grants. It waits.
2. **D5a, the two-thread check:** the process must have exactly its own thread and the admin thread, or it refuses to start. A site process has no `/proc` (A4), so the sandbox mode opens `/proc/self/task` before it confines the process and keeps it at `TASKS_FD` (`CONTROL_FD + 1`, which its `close_range` spares). The site process counts its threads by it (`threads_of`) and closes it.
3. **The narrowing:** its own thread narrows itself to the narrow rules the front hands over (`Spec::narrow`, in `LICHEN_SANDBOX_NARROW`), with lichen's one ruleset builder (`narrow_this_thread`). It is Landlock only, so the egress's synchronised seccomp filter still finds one chain on every thread.
4. **The main runtime** is built by that narrowed thread. Every worker, blocking thread and child is narrowed by inheritance, and each child keeps 1a's nested layer.
5. **D5b, the thread-making globals:** the watchdog's patrol and the SSR and panes sweeps are touched there, so none is first made by the admin thread with its grants.
6. **Only then is the admin thread let go.** It does nothing yet but serve a test server's probe; from unit 3 it serves the admin router.

**What changes now, and what later:**
- **Until unit 3 grants the admin area,** the narrow rules are the site process's grants (`front.rs`, `site_spec`). The order is in place before there is anything for it to hold back.
- **An unconfined site process** (local modes) is handed no rules: it starts its admin thread all the same, one shape, and narrows nothing.
- **A test server** may grant an admin-only folder (`LICHEN_TEST_ADMIN_ONLY`), and the site probe reads each path on both sides (`admin_reads`).

About 380 product lines, within unit 1's budget of 1,300.

---

Tests for FULL-SITE-PROCESS unit 1b, for #1613.

- **`a_site_processs_main_runtime_is_narrowed_and_its_admin_thread_is_not`** (lichen-cli): a test server grants the site process an admin-only folder that its narrow rules leave out.
  - The probe's read on the main runtime is refused (`PermissionDenied`).
  - The same read on the admin thread succeeds (`ok`).
  - The site's own file is read on both sides.

  This is unit 0's probe g as a test.
- **`a_site_process_is_contained_in_one_place`** (workspace_structure): only `site_process_main` narrows a thread or starts the admin thread. The admin thread's code reaches no main-runtime task, blocking pool or handle, no main watchdog, no child and no git (D1, D5, E4). Each needle, planted, is found.
- **`the_sandbox_and_the_network_are_set_in_named_places`:** `ruleset::restrict_self` has a second caller in `sandbox.rs`, the narrowing.
- **SANDBOX.md's crossings table:** `LICHEN_SANDBOX_NARROW` and `LICHEN_SANDBOX_TASKS_FD`, confined only (`a_site_processs_environment_is_the_tables` reads them in a confined site process's environment, and in no unconfined one).
- **The boundary grants:**
  - six new owners, each with its own reason;
  - `run_child`'s capabilities: `calls:workspace-io` replaced by `io:open`, the thread list opened before confinement. Its reason is extended to say so;
  - hash only: `lichen_cli::main`, `restrict_self` and `probe::probe`.

FULL-SITE-PROCESS unit 1b: `site_process_main`, the admin thread and the narrow sandbox. This is the plan's "containment in one place". Design: `machine-docs/plans/FULL-SITE-PROCESS-U0-DESIGN-2026-10-26.md`, checked SATISFIED.

A site process now starts in this order (`lichen-site/src/site_process/start.rs`). `lichen-cli`'s `main` hands it over after `preamble`.
1. **The admin thread** (`site_process/admin.rs`) starts first, so it keeps the site process's grants. It waits.
2. **D5a, the two-thread check:** the process must have exactly its own thread and the admin thread, or it refuses to start. A site process has no `/proc` (A4), so the sandbox mode opens `/proc/self/task` before it confines the process and keeps it at `TASKS_FD` (`CONTROL_FD + 1`, which its `close_range` spares). The site process counts its threads by it (`threads_of`) and closes it.
3. **The narrowing:** its own thread narrows itself to the narrow rules the front hands over (`Spec::narrow`, in `LICHEN_SANDBOX_NARROW`), with lichen's one ruleset builder (`narrow_this_thread`). It is Landlock only, so the egress's synchronised seccomp filter still finds one chain on every thread.
4. **The main runtime** is built by that narrowed thread. Every worker, blocking thread and child is narrowed by inheritance, and each child keeps 1a's nested layer.
5. **D5b, the thread-making globals:** the watchdog's patrol and the SSR and panes sweeps are touched there, so none is first made by the admin thread with its grants.
6. **Only then is the admin thread let go.** It does nothing yet but serve a test server's probe; from unit 3 it serves the admin router.

**What changes now, and what later:**
- **Until unit 3 grants the admin area,** the narrow rules are the site process's grants (`front.rs`, `site_spec`). The order is in place before there is anything for it to hold back.
- **An unconfined site process** (local modes) is handed no rules: it starts its admin thread all the same, one shape, and narrows nothing.
- **A test server** may grant an admin-only folder (`LICHEN_TEST_ADMIN_ONLY`), and the site probe reads each path on both sides (`admin_reads`).

About 380 product lines, within unit 1's budget of 1,300.

---

Notes, not findings:

- D5a's refusal (a third thread before the narrowing) and D5b's touch of the three sweeps are held by reading and the structure test, but no runtime test plants either. A test-routes hook that starts one extra thread before site_process_main, with the process expected to refuse, would pin D5a cheaply.

Round 2 is SATISFIED or a final bounded list.

record.body:
Fixes the filed gap that blocked the VTOL-elevation integration scenario: the pathfinder recorded a flier's elevation in `Reach` but `steps_to` emitted only FORWARDS/BACKWARDS/TURN_*, so a climb or descent could not reach the server. The emitter now replays the search's `(stand, elevation)` predecessor chain in order: elevation ±1 becomes `UP`/`DOWN`, a facing change becomes a turn, a hex change becomes forwards/backwards, and any chain the rules cannot express (two levels at once, or a hex-and-height change) refuses rather than emitting a wrongly priced route. Ground and jump paths go through the unchanged code, and the candidate builder now passes the scored `Reach` so an altitude cannot be lost between scoring and the wire.

Verification: six new tests plus a stand-route climb test cover two-level climbs, descents, `UP,FORWARDS,UP` ordering, refused chains, ground output identity for every reach, and a real obstacle route that emits `UP,UP,FORWARDS`. The Rust workspace, 772 Python tests and `prek --all-files` pass; no Java change.

The emitter alone does not make the live scenario pass: production `generate` still builds every unit with `Walker::running`, whose mode is Ground, and the climb expansion is gated on Fly. The epic records that the follow-up is to construct a flying walker for VTOLs in candidate generation; until then the integration scenario stays blocked on that, not on `steps_to`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

record.body:
Tests for FULL-SITE-PROCESS unit 1b, for #1613.

- **`a_site_processs_main_runtime_is_narrowed_and_its_admin_thread_is_not`** (lichen-cli): a test server grants the site process an admin-only folder that its narrow rules leave out.
  - The probe's read on the main runtime is refused (`PermissionDenied`).
  - The same read on the admin thread succeeds (`ok`).
  - The site's own file is read on both sides.

  This is unit 0's probe g as a test.
- **`a_site_process_is_contained_in_one_place`** (workspace_structure): only `site_process_main` narrows a thread or starts the admin thread. The admin thread's code reaches no main-runtime task, blocking pool or handle, no main watchdog, no child and no git (D1, D5, E4). Each needle, planted, is found.
- **`the_sandbox_and_the_network_are_set_in_named_places`:** `ruleset::restrict_self` has a second caller in `sandbox.rs`, the narrowing.
- **SANDBOX.md's crossings table:** `LICHEN_SANDBOX_NARROW` and `LICHEN_SANDBOX_TASKS_FD`, confined only (`a_site_processs_environment_is_the_tables` reads them in a confined site process's environment, and in no unconfined one).
- **The spawn goldens** (lichen-adversary's round 1, finding 1): `Spec` gained `narrow`, so the four goldens whose spawns carry a `Spec` record it. Their diff is `narrow` alone, and it narrows nothing:
  - the site process's equals its own `read_only` and `read_write`, until unit 3 grants the admin area to the admin thread alone;
  - the hub's two, the backup's three and the push's one are `null`.

  The grant lists are unchanged.
- **The boundary grants:**
  - six new owners, each with its own reason;
  - `run_child`'s capabilities: `calls:workspace-io` replaced by `io:open`, the thread list opened before confinement. Its reason is extended to say so;
  - hash only: `lichen_cli::main`, `restrict_self` and `probe::probe`.

---

record.body:
Fixes the filed gap that blocked the VTOL-elevation integration scenario: the pathfinder recorded a flier's elevation in `Reach` but `steps_to` emitted only FORWARDS/BACKWARDS/TURN_*, and candidate generation built every unit with a ground walker, so no VTOL climb existed to emit. `steps_to` now replays the search's `(stand, elevation)` chain in order: ±1 level becomes `UP`/`DOWN`, a facing change becomes a turn, a hex change becomes forwards/backwards, and chains the rules cannot express refuse rather than emit a wrongly priced route. `Walker::sweeping` selects `Mode::Fly` for fliers (ground and jump unchanged), and `Walker::flying` carries the unit's own elevation. The candidate sweep, the reach ordering and the stand identity all include elevation, so multi-altitude states are deterministic.

Tests: two-level climbs, descents, `UP,FORWARDS,UP` ordering, refused two-level or hex-and-height chains, ground output identity for every reach, a real obstacle route emitting `UP,UP,FORWARDS`, a VTOL menu containing a climb/dive, every emitted flier route replaying to a priced state, and a Mek's menu byte-identical to the legacy running+jumping pipeline. Rust, 772 Python tests and prek pass; the host already accepts the step names, so no Java change.

The remaining caveat is recorded in the epic: scoring is not yet altitude-aware (`Posture::survey` traces at elevation 0, `Mover::presence` uses the deployed elevation, `StandGroups` does not split by altitude), so a climb is now a legal candidate but its line-of-sight/position features do not value the height. The `vtol-elevation` integration assertion can drop its movement blocker; preferring a climb over a ridge needs the altitude-aware scoring follow-up.
